methods.label: Count by position in the cube
methods.explanation:
Count smaller cubes by their positions, since adding shaded squares directly could count a cube more than once. There are three smaller cubes along each edge, so an exterior cube is at a corner, at the middle of an edge, or at the center of a face.

The visible left face has its four corner squares and its center shaded. Its opposite face has the same pattern. These two opposite faces contain all \(8\) corner cubes and contribute \(2\) face-center cubes.

The visible right face has its four edge-middle squares shaded. Its opposite face contributes four more. Opposite faces share no cubes, so this gives \(2\times4=8\) distinct edge-middle cubes.

The top face has only its center shaded, and the bottom has the same pattern. These contribute \(2\) more face-center cubes.

These groups do not overlap: corner cubes, edge-middle cubes, and face-center cubes occupy different positions. They also account for every shaded square on all six faces. The interior cube has no exterior face to shade. Therefore the total is
\[
8+2+8+2=\boxed{20},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
methods.levelReason: The argument uses elementary spatial reasoning, disjoint categories, and repeated groups of four. It requires no formal inclusion-exclusion or advanced counting.
